title: Spring MVC & REST API Development — Revision

sections.title: Why this module matters
sections.body: REST API design is tested in every Java fullstack fresher interview because it is the primary output of a backend developer. Interviewers expect you to know the correct HTTP verbs, status codes, and how Spring MVC routes requests — mistakes here signal lack of hands-on experience. Global exception handling and bean validation show maturity beyond writing happy-path code.

sections.title: Mental model
sections.body:
- **REST** = architectural style: stateless, client-server, uniform interface (resources identified by URIs, manipulated via HTTP verbs)
- **@RestController** = @Controller + @ResponseBody — every method return value is written directly to the HTTP response body as JSON
- **@RequestMapping** = maps a URL path (and optionally HTTP method) to a handler method; shortcut annotations: @GetMapping, @PostMapping, etc.
- **@RequestBody** = deserialise the HTTP request body JSON into a Java object
- **@PathVariable / @RequestParam** = extract values from the URI path or query string
- **@Valid** = trigger Bean Validation on a method parameter; MethodArgumentNotValidException fires on failure
- **@ControllerAdvice** = global cross-cutting concern class; @ExceptionHandler methods inside catch exceptions from any controller
- **ResponseEntity<T>** = full control over status code, headers, and body in the response
- **HTTP Status Codes** = 2xx success, 4xx client error, 5xx server error — knowing which to return is non-negotiable

sections.title: Must-know concepts
sections.body:
- `rest-fundamentals` — drill: 6 REST constraints, idempotency (GET/PUT/DELETE = idempotent; POST is not), Richardson Maturity Model levels
- `spring-controllers-mapping` — drill: @GetMapping vs @RequestMapping(method=GET), @RestController vs @Controller, produces/consumes media types
- `request-params-path-variables` — drill: /users/{id} uses @PathVariable; /users?page=1 uses @RequestParam; when each is appropriate
- `request-response-body` — drill: @RequestBody triggers Jackson deserialization, @JsonIgnore prevents field serialisation, ResponseEntity gives status code control
- `bean-validation` — drill: @Valid on parameter, @NotNull/@NotBlank/@Size, validation failure returns 400 via MethodArgumentNotValidException
- `global-exception-handling` — drill: @ControllerAdvice + @ExceptionHandler pattern, ProblemDetail for RFC 9457 error response
- `http-status-codes` — drill: 200 vs 201 vs 204, 400 vs 422, 401 vs 403, 404 vs 500 — when to return each
- `comparisons` — drill: PUT replaces entire resource; PATCH modifies specific fields; @PathVariable for resource ID, @RequestParam for filters/pagination
- `scenario-based` — drill: design CRUD endpoints for /products, handle validation errors, paginated list response design

sections.title: Likely interview hooks
sections.body:
- "What is REST? Is every HTTP API RESTful?" → REST has 6 constraints; most APIs are just HTTP-based, not truly RESTful (Richardson level 2 is common)
- "What is the difference between @Controller and @RestController?" → @RestController adds @ResponseBody to every method automatically
- "How does @Valid work in Spring?" → triggers javax/jakarta Bean Validation; MethodArgumentNotValidException if constraints fail
- "How do you handle exceptions globally in Spring Boot?" → @ControllerAdvice class with @ExceptionHandler methods per exception type
- "When do you return 201 vs 200?" → 201 Created after a successful POST that creates a resource; include Location header with the new resource URL

sections.title: Speaking template
sections.body: > *"In my Spring Boot projects I use @RestController to mark the controller layer, then @GetMapping, @PostMapping and so on to map HTTP verbs to methods. Input comes in via @RequestBody for the request body or @PathVariable for URL segments, and I use @Valid to trigger bean validation automatically. For errors I have a @ControllerAdvice class with @ExceptionHandler methods that return a consistent error response body — this keeps every controller clean and focused only on the happy path."*
